goldens.comment: Using retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1 reads a possibly stale value and can lose increments under concurrency; consider an atomic increment via Prisma (increment: 1) to avoid race conditions (also applies to the similar update in the catch block).
goldens.reasoning: C1 raises the same problem: a stale retryCount value can lose increments when runs overlap.

goldens.comment: The deletion logic in scheduleSMSReminders.ts incorrectly deletes non-SMS workflow reminders (e.g., Email, WhatsApp) that have retryCount > 1. This occurs because the retryCount condition within the OR clause for deletion lacks a method: WorkflowMethods.SMS filter, causing it to apply to all reminder types instead of only SMS reminders, which is the intended scope of this function.
goldens.reasoning: C2 points out the same missing SMS method filter, which lets non-SMS reminders be deleted.

candidates: `retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1` is based on a potentially stale in-memory value; if this cron overlaps/runs concurrently it can lose increments

The `retryCount > 1` branch isn't scoped to `method: SMS`, so it will delete any WorkflowReminder that happens to have retryCount incremented (even non-SMS methods), causing potential unintended data loss
`update()` will throw if the reminder was deleted between `findMany` and this write, which would escape the catch block - needs to be robust to concurrency and missing rows
